candidate_relations.reason: Accessory extraocular muscle matches the stable linear orbital band with extraocular-muscle signal parallel to medial rectus.
Orbital lymphangioma is a vascular malformation, not a muscle-isointense linear band unchanged over years.
Post-excision scar is a related explanation but conflicts with muscle-identical enhancement of a persistent anomalous band.
Orbital mass is a generic parent and omits the accessory extraocular-muscle identity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: generic orbital mass missing accessory muscle

candidate_relations.reason: Orbital lymphoma is a progressive neoplasm, unlike a decades-stable muscle-signal band without proptosis.
Orbital inflammatory disease would not remain unchanged with muscle-identical signal and normal orbital fat.
Adhesion syndrome is a postoperative motility diagnosis that conflicts with an anomalous muscle-signal band.
Strabismus/vertical misalignment is the motility manifestation, not the accessory muscle itself.
Tendonitis is an inflammatory tendon process, not a discrete anomalous extraocular-muscle band.
Adhesional syndrome is the same incompatible postoperative fibrosis explanation as adhesion syndrome.
Muscle fibrosis is a restrictive alternative that conflicts with a parallel muscle-isointense anomalous band.
Thyroid-associated orbitopathy is excluded by absent proptosis and normal retroocular fat.
Extraocular muscle names the tissue type but not the supernumerary/accessory muscle diagnosis.
Superior oblique palsy is a different vertical-misalignment mechanism from an accessory medial band with elevation deficit.
Orbital dermoid cyst is a developmental cystic mass, not a linear muscle-signal band.
Duane syndrome is a congenital innervation disorder, not an anomalous extraocular-muscle band on MRI.
Orbital pseudotumor is inflammatory and would not be a decades-stable muscle-isointense linear lesion.
Those congenital motility syndromes are related but incompatible with a discrete accessory extraocular-muscle band.
Idiopathic orbital inflammation conflicts with unchanged muscle-signal anatomy and normal fat.
Congenital extraocular muscle hypoplasia is the opposite anatomic abnormality from an accessory muscle.
